data.title: Pick the route
data.ask: Approve the strategy and one route. Nothing downstream is built until you do.
open_questions: Is this a generated job, or do you want it shot live in a real kitchen (A1)?
Can Solace send a sample or all-sides photos of the dripper, with glaze close-ups and a shot of it sitting on a mug (A5, A21)?
Is the tape line across the doorway the right reason nobody interrupts, or should the family's restraint stay unexplained (A3)?
Does 'one cup at a time' describe the glazing or the brew (A6)?
Does Solace sell from its own site with a cart we can track (A8)?

strategy.proposition: The morning queues until the last drop leaves ceramic glazed by hand. (Replaces key_message: no F# supports its duration, 'ten minutes' (A7), or its superlative, 'only'.)
strategy.tension: Who: parents who make coffee by hand on school mornings (kettle, hand grinder, a dripper or another hand brewer). They stand at the counter with their back to the kitchen doorway while the morning's asks arrive before the school run: a slip to sign, a shoe to find, a banana to peel. They buy a new dripper when the old one chips or cracks, or when someone gives them one (H8, a guess). The media proxy is in assumptions (S2). In their voice: I'd never tell my kids to wait for me, yet the few minutes at the counter when nobody needs me are the ones I'd hate to give up. [H1, a guess, not a verbatim] The pull: being the parent who is always available, against guarding one stretch where they aren't needed. What they'd hate to admit: that they want the family to wait. Asking why once past 'time', the loss isn't minutes; it's the one part of the morning when they are nobody's next task. Take the product away and it still holds: this is about a parent and a family, not coffee gear. The scene it gives the CD: her back to a doorway where the whole morning is already standing, and at their feet the ghost of an older line 40 cm nearer the counter (A19). The queue once stood closer, and she has won that ground back: the wish they'd hate to admit, laid down in tape.

routes.central_idea: Behind the tape, the morning waits on a dripper glazed by hand, not on her.
routes.emotional_promise: The guilt-free relief of a clack, not a word from her, sending the whole queue over the tape at once.
routes.product_role: Job: the household's clock. The queue waits on the dripper, not on her. If the drip is audible from the doorway (A16), the row in B rocks forward on each drip and lifts its heels together on the longest gap. The last drop, the lift and the clack then open the line. Under the A16 fallback the queue waits on the clack alone. That is still the dripper's sound, not a word or a look from her, so the line stays true, and the last drop is held on screen 17 frames before the lift. The dripper is a tool first (set on the mug, bloomed, poured through, dripping) and becomes the hero only in the end frame. First appearance: D01 at 0:03 in A, in use on the lopsided mug (skippable 16:9, inside 5 s); D02/D03 at 0:02 (vertical, inside 3 s); D04 at 1.2 s on the proposed timing (1.5 s on development's); sharp in D05 and in D06 frame 2. Handling: she lifts it by the handle or flange the reference shows (A5) and sets it down flat, base ring to board: a firm contact, not a drop. No bare fingertips on a just-brewed cone (that would imply a heat claim) and no drop (that would imply a chip claim, and chipping is H8's replacement trigger). Brand assets and where they sit: the dripper's own form and glaze, taken from the reference only (A5), with no generated glaze detail. 'Solace. Glazed by hand.' over D01's end frame at 56-60 s, in the lower third at frame right, 66-78% down: above the skip button's corner and clear of the dripper and the mug. 'Solace' and '$38' over the D02/D03 end frame at 18-20 s, left of centre, 20-30% down, above the dripper and mug (about 35-57% down), clear of the top 14%, the bottom 25-35% and the right 12%. Burned-in sound captions sit left of centre: 58-64% down in A (on the board in front of the mug) and 20-28% down in B (over the queue's knees). That keeps them clear of the tape at 57%, the ghost line at 63% and every UI zone. 'Solace' on D04 at 4.5-6 s and in D05's lower third. 'Solace' on both D06 frames, '$38' on frame 2 only. No logo card and no URL super. Proof: 'Solace makes a $38 ceramic pour-over dripper'; 'glazed by hand'. Held back: 'one cup at a time' (A6). Implies nothing further: no super or caption sits beside the full mug, the drip or the pour, so nothing reads as a heat, capacity, brew-time, dishwasher or origin claim. The bracketed sound captions name a sound and nothing else. No scale in frame, so no readout and no grams. Rival test: a rival cone would make the same clack. It would not carry the line's 'glazed by hand', or the end frame's glaze-to-glaze rhyme with a mug a child glazed. That rhyme holds only if the reference shows hand variation (A5).
routes.execution_example: SAFE. Costs the belief that a parent's pause lasts only as long as she can defend it: here the dripper holds it, not her. Keeps: all of Lucas's seed and the developed premise; 'ten minutes' stays off screen (A7). Adds one beat, a question for Lucas: the row's heels lift together on the drawdown's longest gap (40-44 s), only if A16 holds. Casting: a mother because the seed names one (A11). The partner's hands are full (the toddler on his hip, the school bag), so what queues is the children's asks, and the rule guards the making, not her role. A11's swap (father at the counter, partner becomes mother) plays every beat unchanged. Flagged for claims review (UK CAP/BCAP harmful-gender-stereotype rules). Look: two locked positions (A: 28 mm, lens 5 cm above a 90 cm counter, 40 cm from the dripper, focus fixed on it at T4; B: 24 mm, 10 cm off the floor); overcast back-door key frame left, 6000K, 3:1; tape #3B7FC4 on mid-oak #8F6B47, heather socks #C4C6C8, navy trainer #1E2B45, banana #E6C84A; no scale; source sound, no music. Tags: G generated from text; R from the reference Solace has yet to supply (A5); C composite. No P beats: the route is generated (A1) and no shoot budget is authorized. Every A frame holds the dripper sharp, so every A beat carries R, and none generates until A5 arrives. Week 1 runs only the B plates, the soft-doorway plates and a drip-legibility test on a plain grey placeholder cone (four 9:16 generations judged on a phone; a test plate, never cut into a deliverable). If there is no reference by the end of week 1, the A tests slip and Lucas is told. D01, 60 s, 16:9: 0-3 s [G] B: the empty tape, its middle scuffed blue-grey, and the pale ghost line 40 cm nearer. 0-1.2 s, the tap runs into the kettle; at 1.3 s the switch clicks, then only the element's first tick and hiss; at 2.0 s heather-grey socks skid in and stop on the tape. 3-7 s [R+G; fallback C: R dripper plate with G hands] A: the kettle's rumble comes in full on the cut; her hands set the dripper on the lopsided mug's high points; the slip and pen are held out soft behind. 7-11 s [R+G; fallback R+G: spooning pre-ground coffee from a tin (A20)] A: the grinder's crunch; a small figure hops into the soft doorway. 11-14 s [G] B: a sock-foot and one untied navy trainer land on the tape; its pair lies under the table edge at frame left. 14-20 s [R+G; fallback R: locked on the spout and rim, no hands] A: the kettle clicks off; the bloom pour; the grounds hiss; the kettle goes back on its base with a plastic click, never on the board; the partner arrives soft behind, the toddler's banana held out like the slip. 20-23 s [G] B: brown felt slippers join the row. 23-30 s [R+G; fallback R: no hands, spout and rim only; last resort C: a G water stream composited over an R dripper plate] A: she pours upright, head never forward of her hands, one continuous pour at real speed; the kettle goes back on its base, click. 30-34 s [G] B: the son's toe crosses the tape and snaps back; a heather-grey sock steps in beside it. The hood hook is never shown. 34-40 s [R+G; fallback R+C: G drops composited over an R still plate; mug fallback: a thumb-sized notch in a level rim (A21)] A: the drip in the crescent gap, facing the lens at frame centre, each drop lit from frame left against the mug's shadowed inside, slowing. 40-44 s [G; A16 fallback G: the row toeing the tape in room tone, no heel lift] B: each drip is heard from the doorway, and the row's weight rocks forward on each one. The gaps stretch. At 43.4 s, on a gap longer than any before, every heel lifts together and holds. Cut to A at 44.0 s on that lift. 44-48 s [R+G; fallback C: R product plate over a G soft-doorway plate, clack on the set-down frame] A: two seconds with no drop. The last drop falls at 46.1 s and holds on screen 17 frames. The lift begins at 46.8 s, by the handle or flange the reference shows (A5). At 47.6 s she sets it down flat, base ring to board: a firm contact, not a drop. Clack, and the soft doorway begins emptying forward in the same frame. Cut at 48.0 s, 10 frames after the clack. 48-51 s [G] B: every foot crosses at once, picked up mid-stride on the first lurch; feet, a chair scrape, a zip and a bag dropped. 51-55 s [R+G; fallback C: three G hand-and-object plates keyed in at her elbow over an R dripper-and-mug plate; if hands still fail, the slip alone plus the trainer's laces entering frame] A: without turning, she points under the table. The slip, the trainer with its laces trailing and the banana reach her elbow on forearms from beyond the frame's side edges; no face, no eye line. 55-60 s [R+G+C; fallback R+C: open after she has gone, only the dripper and the mug, the morning moving off in sound] A: the morning carries her out of frame, leaving the dripper, still wet, beside the full lopsided mug on the board, at the same scale and height, glaze to glaze; 'Solace. Glazed by hand.' at 56-60 s. CTA: the Solace product page (own-site cart, A8) through the platform's click-through; no URL or 'shop' super. D02 (the To, 20 s, 9:16): 0-2 s [G] B: heather-grey socks enter at 0 s and stop dead on the tape by 1.0 s, toes curled over its counter-side edge. The tap runs to 0.7 s, the switch clicks at 0.8 s, and '[kettle rumbling]' lands on the element's first tick at 0.9 s. 2-6 s [R+G] A: the pour; the dripper is in frame from 2.0 s; the slip and pen are held out soft behind. 6-9 s [G] B: the socks on the tape, toes curling over its edge. 9-12 s [R+G; fallback as D01 34-40 s] A: the drip in the crescent gap, the slip still held out soft behind, '[drip]'. 12-14 s [R+G] A: the release, with a 14-frame hold: last drop 12.2 s, lift 12.8 s, set-down 13.4 s, '[clack]', the doorway beginning to empty forward, cut at 14.0 s. 14-15 s [G] B: the grey socks cross first. 15-20 s [R+G+C; fallback C: G pen-and-hand plate over an R dripper plate] A: the daughter's forearm, from beyond the frame's right edge (more than 30 cm off her mother's centre line), lands the slip blank side up beside the dripper. Her mother's hand signs it with the daughter's pen, framed from her hand's side so the strokes stay under the palm and only the pen's movement reads. Slip and hand leave; 'Solace' and '$38' at 18-20 s. D03 opens on the sock-foot landing beside the untied trainer by 0.8 s. At 16-20 s the trainer reaches her elbow on the son's forearm from beyond the frame edge. Shortest cut (D04, 6 s, from D01 footage; timing proposed to development and the strategist): 0-1.2 s B, the row rocking on a drip, heels lifting together at 0.6 s and holding, '[drip]' (A16 fallback: room tone, no heel lift, '[drip]' moved to 1.2 s over A). 1.2-3.2 s A, last drop at 1.3 s, a 17-frame hold, lift at 2.0 s, clack at 2.8 s, then 10 frames of the doorway beginning to empty, '[clack]'. 3.2-4.5 s B, every foot crosses. 4.5-6.0 s the end frame, 'Solace'. The turn stays intact; the dripper is on screen from 1.2 s and readable for 2.0 s before the end frame. Both criterion-5 panel versions are re-issued on this timing. Tests: competitor swap: a rival cone makes the same clack and the same queue. R1 holds against it only through 'glazed by hand', in the line and in the glaze-to-glaze end frame, which needs A5's hand variation. Pairing: R1's example times the queue to the drip (the rocking, the heel lift) and keeps the line once, with the seed's toe hauled back. It has no false ending, no tape pressed flat, no lace drawn back, no present and no giver-first queue, so it plays neither R2's idea nor R3's. All three share the clack release because it is a must-include; the test runs on everything else. Muted in 3 s: in D02 0-1.0 s, heather-grey socks stop dead on a blue line with a pale strip in front of them, which reads as a house rule before any caption; the dripper follows at 2 s.

routes.central_idea: Her pause isn't taken from the family; they keep it for her, down to the tape.
routes.emotional_promise: The sheepish comfort of being backed: a sister's toe pressing the lifting tape flat as her brother's is hauled back off the old line.
routes.product_role: Job: what the family keeps the line for, and the board their deal is settled on. It is not their clock. In this route the queue never listens for the drip: it stays in A's close sound by design, so R2 needs nothing from A16. The family knows which sound counts. When the kettle comes down on the board in the bloom with a heavy, dull thump, the son tests the line and his sister holds it. Only the dripper's short, dry tock opens it. Then the slip is countersigned, blank side up, on the board beside the still-wet dripper, so the product sits inside the settlement in D01 as well as D02 (the strategy's reason D02 carries the To). It is a tool through the brew and the hero only in the end frame. First appearance: D01 at 0:03 in A (skippable 16:9, inside 5 s); D02/D03 at 0:02 (vertical, inside 3 s); D04 at 1.2 s (proposed timing). Handling: lifted by the handle or flange the reference shows (A5) and set down flat, base ring to board: a firm contact, not a drop (no heat or chip implication). Brand assets and where they sit: the dripper's form and glaze, from the reference only (A5). 'Solace. Glazed by hand.' over D01's end frame at 56-60 s, lower third, frame right, above the skip button's corner. 'Solace' and '$38' over the D02/D03 end frame at 18-20 s, left of centre, 20-30% down, clear of the top 14%, bottom 25-35% and right 12% UI zones. Sound captions as in R1 (58-64% down in A, 20-28% down in B). 'Solace' on D04 at 4.5-6 s, in D05's lower third and on both D06 frames; '$38' on D06 frame 2. No logo card. Proof: 'Solace makes a $38 ceramic pour-over dripper'; 'glazed by hand'. Held back: 'one cup at a time' (A6). The bloom's pause is shown but never timed or captioned (A7); it is category knowledge (H5), not a Solace claim. No super or caption sits beside the full mug, the drip or the pour. No scale in frame. Rival test: a rival cone could sit on the same board. What holds is the family's keeping, the slip signed beside the wet dripper and the glaze-to-glaze end frame, which depends on A5.
routes.execution_example: STRETCH. Costs the belief that wanting the family to wait is selfish, something taken from them: here they keep it for her. Keeps: the uninterrupted making, the tape and its ghost line, the queue growing stage by stage (socks at the kettle, the trainer at the grinder, the slippers at the bloom), the toe hauled back and the sock stepping in, the clack, the point under the table and the full mug. Changes (yes/no questions for Lucas, in assumptions): the toe gag moves from the pour to the bloom's pause and lands on the ghost line. The kettle comes down on the board in the bloom as a false ending. The grinder is heard, not seen, in D01. The sister presses the tape flat and draws a lace back. The signing joins the point in D01's release. Casting: a mother because the seed names one (A11). The partner's hands are full, so what queues is the children's asks. A11's swap plays every beat unchanged. Flagged for claims review (UK CAP/BCAP). Look: B-led and locked, B for 31 of 60 s (B: 24 mm, 10 cm off the floor, both lines always in frame; A: 28 mm, lens 5 cm above a 90 cm counter, 40 cm from the dripper, focus fixed at T4); overcast back-door key frame left, 6000K, a soft graze across the floor, 4:1 at the floor; live tape #3B7FC4, ghost line #D8CCB0, oak floor #8F6B47, heather socks #C4C6C8, brown slippers #7A5A3E; no scale; source sound, thump against tock, no music. Tags: G generated from text; R from the reference pending (A5); C composite; no P beats (A1, no shoot budget). Every A beat carries R and waits for A5. Week 1 runs the B plates, which are most of this route, the soft-doorway plates and the drip-legibility test on a grey placeholder cone (never cut in). If there is no reference by the end of week 1, the A tests slip and Lucas is told. D01, 60 s, 16:9: 0-3 s [G] B: the scuffed blue tape and, 40 cm nearer the lens, the pale ghost line. 0-1.2 s, the tap runs into the kettle; at 1.3 s the switch clicks, then the element's first tick; at 1.5 s heather-grey socks skid in and stop on the live line, the ghost line pale in front of their toes. 3-7 s [R+G; fallback C: R dripper plate with G hands] A: the rumble comes in full on the cut; her hands set the dripper on the lopsided mug; the slip and pen are held out soft behind. 7-16 s [G] B, one held shot: the grinder's crunch is heard over the row. At 8 s a sock-foot and one untied navy trainer land beside the grey socks, its pair under the table edge at frame left. The crunch stops; at 14 s the kettle clicks off; the row shifts its weight. 16-21 s [R+G; fallback R: locked on the spout and rim, no hands] A: the bloom pour; the grounds hiss. At 20 s she sets the kettle down on the board: a heavy, dull thump, water sloshing, the lid rattling, and the pour stops. This is the false ending. 21-28 s [G] B: in the bloom's pause, in room tone, the sock-foot slides over the tape and plants its toe on the ghost line, the old ground; its squeak is the loudest sound. It snaps back (the hood hook is never shown), and a heather-grey sock steps in beside it, its toe pressing the tape's lifting end flat. At 25 s brown felt slippers join the row. 28-35 s [R+G; fallback R: no hands, spout and rim only; last resort C: a G stream over an R dripper plate] A: the kettle rises off the board for the main pour: upright, one continuous pour at real speed. The banana is held out soft behind at the slip's height. She never turns. 35-42 s [G] B, in room tone: the untied trainer's lace has slid across the tape onto her side, and a heather-grey toe draws it back behind the line; the toddler's heel taps her father's hip. 42-46 s [R+G; fallback C: R product plate over a G soft-doorway plate] A: the last drop falls in the crescent gap, facing the lens, at 44.2 s and holds on screen 14 frames. The lift comes at 44.8 s, by the handle or flange the reference shows (A5). At 45.6 s she sets it down flat, base ring to board: a short, dry tock, no slosh. The soft doorway begins emptying forward in the same frame. Cut at 46.0 s, 10 frames after the clack. 46-51 s [G] B: every foot crosses at once, picked up mid-stride; the held noise returns. 51-56 s [R+G+C; fallback C: G pen-and-hand and pointing plates over an R dripper plate] A: the slip lands blank side up on the board beside the wet dripper. Her right hand signs it with the daughter's pen, framed from her hand's side so the strokes stay under the palm and only the pen's movement reads. Without turning, her left hand points down and back under the table, which sets up D03's payoff. The trainer and the banana reach her elbow on forearms from beyond the frame's side edges. 56-60 s [R+G+C; fallback R+C: open after she has gone] A: the dripper, still wet, beside the full lopsided mug, glaze to glaze; 'Solace. Glazed by hand.' at 56-60 s. CTA: the Solace product page through the platform's click-through (A8); no URL super. D02 opens at 0 s as the grey socks enter and stop dead on the tape by 1.0 s, with '[kettle rumbling]' on the element's tick at 0.9 s. The dedicated drawdown shot of the drip in the crescent gap is only in D02 shot 4; in D01 the gap shows just the last drop. D02's release keeps its 14-frame hold (12.2, 12.8 and 13.4 s, cut at 14.0 s). Shortest cut (D04, 6 s, on R2 footage, proposed timing): 0-1.2 s B, the row toeing the tape, '[drip]' carried from the counter as a pre-lap (A16 fallback version: room tone, '[drip]' at 1.2 s over A). 1.2-3.1 s A, last drop at 1.3 s, a 14-frame hold, lift at 1.9 s, '[clack]' at 2.7 s, then 10 frames of the doorway beginning to empty. 3.1-4.5 s B, every foot crosses. 4.5-6.0 s the end frame, 'Solace'. This version carries the release, not the keeping. R2's own variant carries both, and goes to the strategist as a third panel version, not in place of the two: 0-1.6 s B, '[knock]' at 0 s, the toe on the ghost line snaps back and a grey toe presses the tape flat; 1.6-3.5 s A, last drop at 1.7 s, lift at 2.3 s, '[clack]' at 3.1 s; 3.5-4.5 s B, the crossing; 4.5-6.0 s the end frame. In each version the dripper is readable for 1.9 s before the end frame. Tests: competitor swap: a rival cone sits on the same board; the idea holds through the family's keeping and 'glazed by hand' in the end frame (A5). Pairing: R1's example can't play 'they keep it for her, down to the tape': its queue is timed by the drip, and it keeps the line only once. R3's has a giver and a present, not a keeping. R2's example has no drip clock (its queue never hears the drip), so it serves R1's idea only at the shared release. Muted in 3 s: a blue line with a pale strip 40 cm in front of it, and grey socks stopping on the live line, not the old one. That reads as a rule with a history before the dripper appears.

routes.central_idea: Her family's present: a dripper glazed by hand, and their queue moved 40 cm further back.
routes.emotional_promise: The giver's dry pride in queueing first for the present he gave: brown felt slippers on fresh tape, 40 cm behind yesterday's line.
routes.product_role: Job: the present, and what its givers wait on. It comes out of kraft paper the children have scribbled on in red crayon, sealed with strips from the same roll of blue painter's tape that now runs, fresh, across the doorway. Last night the family pulled up the old line and laid a new one 40 cm further from the counter, so the tape, the 40 cm and the dripper read as one present. The partner, who bought it, stands first on the new tape and crosses last. He is the giver and nothing else: the sister's sock, not his slipper, keeps the line, as in the seed. The dripper is a tool first: on the mug at 3 s, bloomed, poured through, dripping. In the end frame it becomes the hero beside the other present on the counter, the lopsided mug her eldest glazed: two presents glazed by hand, one of them by a child. First appearance: D01 at 0:03 in A, already on the mug with the paper open beside it (skippable 16:9, inside 5 s); the unwrapping is heard over B, never seen. D02/D03 at 0:02 (vertical, inside 3 s); D04 at 1.2 s (proposed timing). Handling: lifted by the handle or flange the reference shows (A5) and set down flat, base ring to board: a firm contact, not a drop. Brand assets and where they sit: the dripper's form and glaze, from the reference only (A5). There is no Solace box or branded packaging: the present comes in the children's paper, so nothing generated carries the name. Supers as in R1: 'Solace. Glazed by hand.' at 56-60 s, lower third, frame right, above the skip button's corner; 'Solace' and '$38' at 18-20 s, 20-30% down, left of centre; sound captions at 58-64% down in A and 20-28% down in B; 'Solace' on D04, D05 and both D06 frames; '$38' on D06 frame 2. The paper's corner and its blue seal stay at the end frame's left edge, clear of the supers. Proof: 'Solace makes a $38 ceramic pour-over dripper'; 'glazed by hand'. Held back: 'one cup at a time' (A6). Implies nothing further: the paper is the family's, so there is no gift-box, gift-service or packaging claim. No price sits on the present, no super or caption sits beside the full mug, the drip or the pour, and there is no scale in frame. Rival test: a rival cone could come out of the same paper. The idea is about the giver, so against a rival it holds only through 'glazed by hand' and the two-presents end frame, which needs A5's hand variation. It is no harder to copy than R1; what it changes is who buys.
routes.execution_example: BRAVE. Costs the belief that a present is paid for once, at the till: its givers pay for this one every morning, 40 cm further back. Keeps: the uninterrupted making from the kettle to the last drop, the tape and its ghost line, the queue growing stage by stage, the toe over the line and the sister's sock stepping in, the clack, the point under the table, the objects at her elbow and the full mug. Changes (yes/no questions for Lucas, in assumptions): this is the dripper's first morning, a present from the family. The ghost line is where the tape ran until last night, and the live line is fresh and unscuffed. The partner is first on the tape and last across. The unwrapping is heard, not seen. His hand takes the banana back. The present's paper stays at the end frame's edge. D03 is proposed as 'The present'. The Who widens to the partner who buys it (H2 flight read). Casting: a mother because the seed names one (A11). Here the partner is the giver, and he takes one ask back at the end, so the work is visibly shared. A11's swap plays every beat unchanged. Flagged for claims review (UK CAP/BCAP). Look: R1's two locked positions (A: 28 mm at T4, lens 5 cm above a 90 cm counter; B: 24 mm, 10 cm off the floor), with B centred on the slippers; overcast back-door key frame left, 6000K, 3:1; fresh tape #3B7FC4, kraft #C4A57A, red crayon #C8413B, slippers #7A5A3E, banana #E6C84A; no scale; source sound with the rip and the paper's crackle, no music. Tags: G generated from text; R from the reference pending (A5); C composite; no P beats (A1, no shoot budget). Every A beat carries R and waits for A5. Week 1 runs the B plates, the soft-doorway plates, the drip-legibility test on a grey placeholder cone (never cut in) and a studio crayon drawing for the paper. If there is no reference by the end of week 1, the A tests slip and Lucas is told. D01, 60 s, 16:9: 0-3 s [G] B: the fresh blue tape, sharp-edged, and the pale ghost line 40 cm nearer. 0-1.2 s, the tap runs into the kettle; at 1.3 s the switch clicks, then the element's tick. At 1.5 s brown felt slippers step onto the tape at centre frame and stop, the giver first on the line, as the long rip of tape off paper comes from the counter. 3-7 s [R+G+C, with the crayon marks composited from a studio drawing so no generated scribble can turn into letters; fallback R+C: no hands, the dripper on the mug, the paper open beside it, the last strip already off] A: at 3.0 s the dripper is already on the lopsided mug, with the scribbled kraft paper open at frame left, and one hand peels the last strip of blue tape off its fold. The paper crackles; the rumble comes in full. data.recommendation: Rationale: R1 plays the proposition, 'The morning queues until the last drop leaves ceramic glazed by hand', in one beat: D01 44-48 s, the last drop held 17 frames, the lift, the clack, the doorway lurching forward. The dripper, not her, sets the release (H4); R2 needs H1's admission and R3 needs gift buyers. D02 'The slip' serves 'the share of viewers who can say, unprompted, what the child wanted and when they got it', then 'Solace dripper orders per 1,000 impressions, click-attributed' (criteria 5, 1). Gives up: the admission as the film's spine. In R2 the family keeps her pause down to the tape: the toe hauled off the old line, the tape pressed flat, the lace drawn back, the kettle's thump ignored. In R1 the ghost line is dressing that rewards a second look. R1 also gives up the giver as buyer (R3's slippers first on fresh tape, the 40 cm and the dripper as one present) and a new structure: R1 is the development's film as written, plus the heel lift. Failure (1, the idea's): the last drop at phone size, in D02 9-14 s and D01 44-48 s. At 0.4 m on 28 mm, a 4 mm drop is about 14-16 px wide on a 1080-wide 9:16 screen, inside a crescent gap against dark coffee, and both R1's line and kill test (b) rest on it. Fix: the gap faces the lens at frame centre, and the 6000K key from frame left puts a highlight on the drop against the mug's shadowed inside. Run four week-1 generations of the drip at 9:16 on a grey placeholder cone, judged on a phone (a legibility test, never cut in), and repeat them on the reference when A5 lands. Fallback: the A21 notch. Failure (2): D02 0-1.0 s, B at phone size. The tape can read as a floor stripe before the socks stop on it, and grey socks can vanish into a grey scuff. Fix: the socks enter at 0 s and stop dead by 1.0 s, toes curled over the tape's counter-side edge. The socks are light heather #C4C6C8, the scuff is worn dark blue-grey (about #6E7C8E) on #3B7FC4 tape over #8F6B47 oak, and the ghost line stays pale but in frame at 63%. Run four week-1 generations at 9:16 before any other B shot. Kill test: show the first muted cut (week-1 B plates with boarded A frames, or the first generations once A5 lands) at phone size to 10 parents and ask what let the queue cross. The idea has failed if (a) 3 or more of 10 read fear, punishment or neglect (H4), or (b) 3 or more of 10 answers are coded Fail. Coding frame: a Pass names the coffee finishing, the dripper coming off, or the sound. A Fail names her permission or a signal from her ('when mum was ready', 'she let them'). Two coders score separately, and a disagreement counts as a Fail. An answer that names neither is coded None and doesn't count toward the kill; 3 or more None sends the drop back to Failure (1), a craft fix. Either kill means the dripper has not taken the rule off her: switch to R2, where the family owns the rule and nothing hangs on the drip. Under A16's fallback the line stays true, since the queue waits on the dripper's clack, not on her. The 17-frame hold (last drop 46.1 s, lift 46.8 s, set-down 47.6 s, cut 48.0 s) keeps the drop on screen for (b). Case R2-stretch-ghost-line: strategy.hypotheses H1, second half, at a studio threshold above its survival line (H1 survives at 2 hedgers among those who single the coffee-making out). If 4 or more of all 8 interviewees hedge or apologise for wanting it, unprompted, R2 is the pick. Only the family's keeping answers the admission, so she never has to ask. R2 is also the safer build if development's A16 check finds the drip inaudible from the doorway, since its queue never listens for it. Case R3-brave-the-present: strategy.hypotheses H8 and the H2 flight read. R3 is the pick, at launch or for the next flight, if 4 or more of the 8 interviewees say, unprompted, that the brewer on their counter was a gift (a studio threshold, above H8's kill line of 3 for chip-or-gift combined). It is also the pick if the order-confirmation survey shows most orders are gifts ('the buyer is a partner'). Only R3 speaks to the giver, and with D03 retold as 'The present', the split tests that buyer directly. Conventions (H3's list, a guess, not an audit; listed first in assumptions): (1) an overhead bloom close-up with a slow-motion pour; (2) a gooseneck kettle on a sunlit, spotless counter, with grams and a timer on screen; (3) the lone first sip at a window. R1 breaks all three: the bloom at counter height and real speed; overcast light on a counter with a dish rack and a cable, and no scale at all; no sip, with the mug full to the end. R2 turns (1) into its false ending, heard from the floor. R3 swaps (3)'s lone sip for its givers queueing, first on and last across. The ten one-liners, and why seven were killed, are in assumptions.
